objectives.text: Review RFC 0011 v1.4 line by line for consistency and formal register: every defined term used with one meaning and every term used defined; one name per concept (no synonyms); every section, clause, table, decision id (D874d-<n>, D-DEL<n>) and settled-point id (S-<n>) reference resolves and supports what the sentence says; tables and prose agree; clause numbering is continuous; identifiers are in code format; abbreviations are expanded on first use; and the register is formal technical English (no colloquialisms, contractions, rhetorical phrasing, first person or informal intensifiers). Work in five batches, in this order: sections 1 and 2; 3.1 and 3.2; 3.3 to 3.5; 3.6 to 3.9; sections 4 to 10 and appendix A. After each batch, write your AAR file as a new version holding every finding so far. Report each defect with the RFC line and the exact replacement text.

constraints.text: Read-only: do not edit, commit or push any repository file, and do not comment on or edit any issue or PR. Write only in your scratch directory and your AAR file.

Review in the five batches of OBJ-2, in order. After each batch, write your AAR file as a new version (provenance.version v1.0, v1.1, ...) holding every finding so far, before you start the next batch.
Do not alter a quotation of the commander: quoted text keeps its spelling, spacing and punctuation. Propose changes to the RFC's own prose only.
Do not reopen the commander's decisions (D874d-<n>); a decision you judge unsound is a proposal, not a defect.
Do not repeat a defect that RFC 0011 v1.4 already fixes: v1.4 applied the proposals of missions 874d-7 and 874d-9 (their AAR files are reference artifacts). Report only what v1.4 still has.
Cite every defect by its RFC line number, as read from disk when you start, and quote the text; every proposal gives the exact old text and new text, the old text occurring exactly once in the RFC.

Fetch issue nobul-tech/aitools#180 yourself (gh issue view 180 --repo nobul-tech/aitools, with and without --comments; body v5.5 or later); do not use the copies in the 874d-8 scratch directory, which are stale.
Stop every background shell and monitor you start before you hand back.
